hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: We want purchases made on Fridays in November 2023.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: In MySQL, `dayofweek` returns 6 for Friday, and the week index of November can be derived using the difference between week numbers plus 1.

hints.title: Query Construction
hints.text: Group by purchase_date and aggregate total spending, ordering by week_of_month ascending.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT 
    WEEK(purchase_date, 1) - WEEK('2023-11-01', 1) + 1 AS week_of_month, 
    purchase_date, 
    SUM(amount_spend) AS total_amount 
FROM Purchases 
WHERE DAYOFWEEK(purchase_date) = 6 
  AND MONTH(purchase_date) = 11 
  AND YEAR(purchase_date) = 2023 
GROUP BY purchase_date 
ORDER BY week_of_month;
```

variables: N: total records in Purchases table
complexity.notes: Filter November Fridays followed by single-key aggregation.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full table scans without date index are inefficient.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for aggregation hash tables.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use date-time extractors cleanly to isolate week numbers and Friday days of the week.

solutions.code:
SELECT 
    WEEK(purchase_date, 1) - WEEK('2023-11-01', 1) + 1 AS week_of_month, 
    purchase_date, 
    SUM(amount_spend) AS total_amount 
FROM Purchases 
WHERE DAYOFWEEK(purchase_date) = 6 
  AND MONTH(purchase_date) = 11 
  AND YEAR(purchase_date) = 2023 
GROUP BY purchase_date 
ORDER BY week_of_month;

SELECT 
    (EXTRACT(WEEK FROM purchase_date) - EXTRACT(WEEK FROM DATE '2023-11-01') + 1)::INTEGER AS week_of_month, 
    purchase_date, 
    SUM(amount_spend)::INTEGER AS total_amount 
FROM Purchases 
WHERE EXTRACT(DOW FROM purchase_date) = 5 
  AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM purchase_date) = 11 
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM purchase_date) = 2023 
GROUP BY purchase_date 
ORDER BY week_of_month;
